newsitem.title: USA: Toshiba unveils notebook PC under 2 pounds.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba unveils notebook PC under 2 pounds.

text.p: Toshiba Corp., the world's leading notebook computer maker, said Monday it introduced a new line of lightweight mini-notebooks and unveiled new versions of its existing family of notebook computers.
The company said its new Libretto mini-notebook was intended as a companion to full-sized desktop computers and to be used for mobile communications and information management.
Among the products is a new model, the Libretto 50CT, the first full-function notebook that weighs less than two pounds and runs Microsoft Corp's Windows 95 software. Its list price is $1,999.

In addition, Toshiba unveiled the newest members of its Satellite notebook family, the 220 CDS and 225 CDS, which are aimed at the corporate and consumer markets respectively. Both computers also are priced at $1,999.
In 1996, Toshiba said it held roughly half the U.S. market for portable computers priced under $1,999, citing data from market research firm Audits & Surveys.
Other machines unveiled by Toshiba on Monday include the Portege 300, with a suggested list price of $3,499, and the Satellite Pro 440 Series, starting in the mid-$2,000 range.
Overall, Toshiba remains the top supplier of portable computers, with a 24.4 percent share of the U.S. market in the first quarter of 1997, according to International Data Corp.
Toshiba made the announcements at Spring Comdex/Spring'97, a major computer trade show under way this week in Atlanta.
